paragraphs.title: The Second Tablets and the Ark of the Covenant

easy.question: Who commanded Moses to prepare new tablets?
answers: The Lord
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “The Lord said unto me.”

easy.question: How many stone tablets was Moses commanded to hew?
answers: One tablet
Two tablets
Three tablets
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Moses to hew “two tables of stone.”

easy.question: Where did Moses put the tablets after coming down from the mountain?
answers: In the tent
In his hands
In the ark
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says that Moses put the tablets in the ark.

medium.question: What did Moses do after making the wooden ark and hewing the tablets?
answers: He went up the mountain
He broke the tablets
He gave them to the people
medium.explanation: After making the ark and hewing the tablets, Moses went up the mountain with the tablets in his hands.

medium.question: Why were the same words written on the new tablets as on the first tablets?
answers: Because the first tablets were small
Because the first tablets had been broken
Because the people requested more tablets
medium.explanation: The passage says that the first tablets had been broken, so the words were written again on other tablets.

medium.question: In the phrase “according to the first writing,” what does “writing” mean?
answers: The wording or inscription of the first tablets
The place where they first sat
The first journey
medium.explanation: Here, “writing” refers to the written wording or inscription; the context shows that it matched the first tablets.

challenge.question: Who hewed the tablets, and who wrote the Ten Commandments on them?
answers: Moses hewed them, and the Lord wrote on them
The Lord hewed them, and Moses wrote on them
The people hewed them, and Moses wrote on them
challenge.explanation: Moses says that he hewed the stone tablets, while the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Moses carried the tablets himself when he went up the mountain?
answers: He made a wooden ark
It says, “having the two tables in mine hand”
He came down from the mountain
challenge.explanation: The phrase “having the two tables in mine hand” explicitly says that Moses carried them.

challenge.question: What does the ending, saying that the tablets were in the ark “as the Lord commanded me,” teach?
answers: The tablets were kept in the ark, and Moses obeyed the command
The tablets were immediately given to the people
The ark remained empty
challenge.explanation: Moses put the tablets in the ark as commanded, emphasizing his obedience.

questions.question: Who hewed the tablets, and who wrote the Ten Commandments on them?
answers: Moses hewed them, and the Lord wrote on them
The Lord hewed them, and Moses wrote on them
The people hewed them, and Moses wrote on them
questions.explanation: Moses says that he hewed the stone tablets, while the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Moses carried the tablets himself when he went up the mountain?
answers: He made a wooden ark
It says, “having the two tables in mine hand”
He came down from the mountain
questions.explanation: The phrase “having the two tables in mine hand” explicitly says that Moses carried them.

questions.question: What does the ending, saying that the tablets were in the ark “as the Lord commanded me,” teach?
answers: The tablets were kept in the ark, and Moses obeyed the command
The tablets were immediately given to the people
The ark remained empty
questions.explanation: Moses put the tablets in the ark as commanded, emphasizing his obedience.

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Journeys, Aaron’s Death, and the Role of the Levites

easy.question: Who died and was buried at Mosera?
answers: Aaron
Eleazar
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says, “there Aaron died, and there he was buried.”

easy.question: Where did the Israelites travel from Gudgodah?
answers: Mosera
Jotbath
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The passage says, “from Gudgodah to Jotbath.”

easy.question: What did the Lord command Moses to do?
answers: Stay on the mountain
Build the tabernacle
Rise and travel ahead of the people
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses, “Arise, take thy journey before the people.”

medium.question: What was the order of the journeys described in these verses?
answers: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan, Mosera, Gudgodah, Jotbath
Mosera, Jotbath, Beeroth of the children of Jaakan, Gudgodah
Jotbath, Gudgodah, Mosera, Beeroth of the children of Jaakan
medium.explanation: They traveled first from Beeroth of the children of Jaakan to Mosera, then to Gudgodah, and then to Jotbath.

medium.question: In the phrase “Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren,” what does “inheritance” mean?
answers: A journey through the wilderness
Land or property inherited in the country
A priestly position
medium.explanation: “Inheritance” means land or property; the context says that Levi did not receive territory like the other tribes.

medium.question: Why did Levi have no part or inheritance with the other tribes?
answers: Because Levi did not travel
Because Levi died in the wilderness
Because the Lord was Levi’s inheritance and Levi was chosen for the Lord’s service
medium.explanation: The tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark, serve the Lord, and bless in his name; therefore, the Lord was its inheritance.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Eleazar serving in Aaron’s place?
answers: The priesthood passed from father to son
Eleazar replaced Moses
Aaron served again after his death
challenge.explanation: The statement that Eleazar served “in his stead” shows that the priestly role continued through Aaron’s son.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “at that time also” teach about the Lord’s response to Moses?
answers: The Lord never listened to Moses
The Lord listened to Moses again and did not destroy the people
The Lord commanded Moses to remain on the mountain
challenge.explanation: The word “also” indicates that the Lord listened to Moses once again and therefore did not destroy the people.

challenge.question: Which detail about Jotbath emphasizes that it was a place with water?
answers: It was near Mosera
Aaron was buried there
It was called “a land of rivers of waters”
challenge.explanation: The phrase “a land of rivers of waters” explicitly describes Jotbath as a place with watercourses or springs.

questions.question: What can we infer from Eleazar serving in Aaron’s place?
answers: The priesthood passed from father to son
Eleazar replaced Moses
Aaron served again after his death
questions.explanation: The statement that Eleazar served “in his stead” shows that the priestly role continued through Aaron’s son.

questions.question: What does the phrase “at that time also” teach about the Lord’s response to Moses?
answers: The Lord never listened to Moses
The Lord listened to Moses again and did not destroy the people
The Lord commanded Moses to remain on the mountain
questions.explanation: The word “also” indicates that the Lord listened to Moses once again and therefore did not destroy the people.

questions.question: Which detail about Jotbath emphasizes that it was a place with water?
answers: It was near Mosera
Aaron was buried there
It was called “a land of rivers of waters”
questions.explanation: The phrase “a land of rivers of waters” explicitly describes Jotbath as a place with watercourses or springs.

paragraphs.title: What the Lord Requires of Israel

easy.question: According to verse 12, what does the Lord require of Israel?
answers: To fear him, walk in his ways, love him, and serve him
To build new cities
To leave the land of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says that Israel is to fear the Lord, walk in his ways, love him, and serve him.

easy.question: Why should Israel keep the Lord’s commandments and statutes?
answers: To be strong in war
For their good
So that all nations will serve them
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says that keeping the commandments and statutes is “for thy good.”

easy.question: What belongs to the Lord according to verse 14?
answers: Only the land of Israel
Only the people of Israel
The heavens, the earth, and everything in them
easy.explanation: Verse 14 says that the heavens, the earth, and everything in them belong to the Lord.

medium.question: How does verse 13 relate to the requirements in verse 12?
answers: It explains that keeping the commandments is part of serving the Lord
It cancels the requirements in verse 12
It speaks only about the nations of the land
medium.explanation: Verse 12 presents service to the Lord, and verse 13 further explains it through keeping his commandments and statutes.

medium.question: In the phrase “the Lord had a delight in thy fathers,” what does “delight” mean?
answers: Forgot
Chose them with love and affection
Was angry with them
medium.explanation: Here, “delight” means to desire or take pleasure in someone; the context says that the Lord loved the fathers and chose their descendants.

medium.question: What is the connection between the Lord’s ownership of the world and his choosing Israel?
answers: Because everything belongs to him, he chose Israel from among all peoples
Israel owns the heavens and the earth
The Lord belongs only to one nation, not to the whole world
medium.explanation: Verse 14 emphasizes that everything belongs to the Lord, and verse 15 adds that he chose Israel from among all peoples.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “with all thy heart and with all thy soul” teach about serving the Lord?
answers: Service should be wholehearted and devoted
It is enough to keep one commandment
Service is required only at a particular time
challenge.explanation: The repeated idea of “all” emphasizes complete devotion, both in heart and soul.

challenge.question: What precise distinction appears in verse 15?
answers: The Lord chose only the fathers, not their descendants
The Lord loved the fathers and also chose their descendants—that is, Israel
The Lord chose all peoples equally
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions both the Lord’s love for the fathers and his choice of their descendants, Israel.

challenge.question: What main idea emerges from the contrast between verses 14 and 15?
answers: The Lord is limited to one land, so he chose Israel
The Lord belongs only to heaven, not to earth
Although the Lord owns the whole world, he chose Israel with special love
challenge.explanation: Verse 14 describes the Lord’s rule over all creation, while verse 15 emphasizes his special love and choice of Israel.

questions.question: What does the phrase “with all thy heart and with all thy soul” teach about serving the Lord?
answers: Service should be wholehearted and devoted
It is enough to keep one commandment
Service is required only at a particular time
questions.explanation: The repeated idea of “all” emphasizes complete devotion, both in heart and soul.

questions.question: What precise distinction appears in verse 15?
answers: The Lord chose only the fathers, not their descendants
The Lord loved the fathers and also chose their descendants—that is, Israel
The Lord chose all peoples equally
questions.explanation: The verse mentions both the Lord’s love for the fathers and his choice of their descendants, Israel.

questions.question: What main idea emerges from the contrast between verses 14 and 15?
answers: The Lord is limited to one land, so he chose Israel
The Lord belongs only to heaven, not to earth
Although the Lord owns the whole world, he chose Israel with special love
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes the Lord’s rule over all creation, while verse 15 emphasizes his special love and choice of Israel.

paragraphs.title: An Open Heart Before the Great God

easy.question: What does the verse command Israel to do with the “foreskin of your heart”?
answers: Circumcise it
Hide it
Make it larger
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart.”

easy.question: What are the people told not to do anymore?
answers: Show partiality
Be stiff-necked
Take a bribe
easy.explanation: The verse says, “be no more stiffnecked,” meaning they must no longer be stubborn.

easy.question: How is the Lord described in the verse?
answers: As God of gods and Lord of lords
As the king of one city
As an angel of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse calls the Lord “God of gods, and Lord of lords.”

medium.question: In the phrase “circumcise the foreskin of your heart,” what does “foreskin” represent?
answers: A covering or hardness
Great joy
Deep wisdom
medium.explanation: In this context, “foreskin” represents spiritual hardness that must be removed, like physical foreskin.

medium.question: Why does the passage command the people not to be stiff-necked?
answers: Because the Lord is great and powerful and requires an open, obedient heart
Because they were forbidden to travel in the wilderness
Because the people needed to become wealthy
medium.explanation: The command is followed by a description of the Lord’s greatness, calling the people to stop resisting his will.

medium.question: What connection appears between the description of the Lord and the end of verse 17?
answers: Because he is great, he accepts bribes
Because he is a just judge, he shows no partiality and takes no bribe
Because he is mighty, he does not speak with people
medium.explanation: The verse describes the Lord as great and mighty, then emphasizes that he neither shows partiality nor accepts a bribe.

challenge.question: What is the symbolic meaning of “the foreskin of your heart”?
answers: A heart that is closed and unwilling to listen to the Lord
A heart rejoicing after victory
A physically strong heart
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers not to physical cutting but to removing inner hardness so that one can listen to the Lord.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the phrase “God of gods, and Lord of lords”?
answers: The Lord is equal to all other gods and lords
The Lord is supreme over every other power and authority
The Lord is only the God of rulers
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that the Lord is supreme over all who are called gods or lords.

challenge.question: What idea connects the command about the heart and neck with the description of the Lord as judge?
answers: People must reject stubbornness and act justly, as the Lord does
People should seek power and bribes
People may favor their relatives
challenge.explanation: The passage connects inner change with the Lord’s example: people should not be stubborn or partial but should act justly.

questions.question: What is the symbolic meaning of “the foreskin of your heart”?
answers: A heart that is closed and unwilling to listen to the Lord
A heart rejoicing after victory
A physically strong heart
questions.explanation: The phrase refers not to physical cutting but to removing inner hardness so that one can listen to the Lord.

questions.question: What can we infer from the phrase “God of gods, and Lord of lords”?
answers: The Lord is equal to all other gods and lords
The Lord is supreme over every other power and authority
The Lord is only the God of rulers
questions.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes that the Lord is supreme over all who are called gods or lords.

questions.question: What idea connects the command about the heart and neck with the description of the Lord as judge?
answers: People must reject stubbornness and act justly, as the Lord does
People should seek power and bribes
People may favor their relatives
questions.explanation: The passage connects inner change with the Lord’s example: people should not be stubborn or partial but should act justly.

paragraphs.title: Justice, Compassion, and Love for the Stranger

easy.question: For whom does the Lord execute judgment?
answers: The fatherless and the widow
The king and the priest
The rich and the mighty
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord executes judgment for the fatherless and widow.

easy.question: What does the Lord give the stranger?
answers: Silver and gold
Food and clothing
A house and a field
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord loves the stranger, giving him food and clothing.

easy.question: Why are the Israelites commanded to love the stranger?
answers: Because the stranger is rich
Because the stranger helps Israel
Because the Israelites were also strangers in Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse reminds Israel that they too were strangers in the land of Egypt.

medium.question: What connection is there between loving the stranger and giving him food and clothing?
answers: Love for the stranger includes practical help for his needs
There is no connection between them
The gifts are intended only for the fatherless
medium.explanation: The verse connects love for the stranger with concrete care for food and clothing.

medium.question: In the phrase “loveth the stranger,” who is the stranger?
answers: A wealthy person
A foreigner or resident from another land
Someone who works in the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The context refers to someone who is not a native of the land and therefore needs care and acceptance.

medium.question: How does remembering Egypt strengthen the command to love the stranger?
answers: It teaches that strangers are always dangerous
It explains that the Egyptians had to give Israel fields
It helps Israel identify with the stranger’s situation
medium.explanation: Israel had once lived as strangers, so they could understand the difficulty and show compassion.

challenge.question: What idea is shared by the treatment of the fatherless, widow, and stranger?
answers: People who may lack power or support should be protected and helped
They should be given positions in government
They should be kept away from society
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes responsibility toward people who may be vulnerable or without protection.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “stranger” in “the stranger” and “ye were strangers” emphasize?
answers: That the stranger must leave the land
The connection between the stranger’s situation and Israel’s past
That all Israelites were born in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording connects the stranger in the present with Israel’s experience as strangers in Egypt.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that loving the stranger is not only a feeling but also an action?
answers: The mention of Egypt
The words “Love ye therefore”
Giving him food and clothing
challenge.explanation: Food and clothing are basic needs, so providing them expresses practical care, not merely emotion.

questions.question: What idea is shared by the treatment of the fatherless, widow, and stranger?
answers: People who may lack power or support should be protected and helped
They should be given positions in government
They should be kept away from society
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes responsibility toward people who may be vulnerable or without protection.

questions.question: What does the repetition of “stranger” in “the stranger” and “ye were strangers” emphasize?
answers: That the stranger must leave the land
The connection between the stranger’s situation and Israel’s past
That all Israelites were born in Egypt
questions.explanation: The repeated wording connects the stranger in the present with Israel’s experience as strangers in Egypt.

questions.question: Which detail shows that loving the stranger is not only a feeling but also an action?
answers: The mention of Egypt
The words “Love ye therefore”
Giving him food and clothing
questions.explanation: Food and clothing are basic needs, so providing them expresses practical care, not merely emotion.

paragraphs.title: Fear, Service, and Clinging to the Lord

easy.question: Whom does the verse command the people to fear?
answers: The Lord your God
An earthly king
All the nations
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God.”

easy.question: What does the verse command people to do for the Lord?
answers: Flee from him
Serve him
Hide his name
easy.explanation: It says, “him shalt thou serve.”

easy.question: What did the Lord do for Israel according to the verse?
answers: He gave them a king
He built them a house
He did great and terrible things for them
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord did “these great and terrible things” for Israel.

medium.question: What is the connection between these commands and the Lord being Israel’s God?
answers: They express loyalty and relationship to the Lord
They are meant to distance Israel from the Lord
They concern only warfare
medium.explanation: Fearing, serving, clinging to, and swearing by the Lord’s name express connection and loyalty to him.

medium.question: In “unto him shalt thou cleave,” what does “cleave” mean?
answers: Stay away from him
Remain faithful and close to him
Write his name
medium.explanation: The context shows that “cleave” means to remain faithfully attached and close to the Lord.

medium.question: What order of commands appears in the verse?
answers: Serve, fear, swear, and cling
Cling, swear, fear, and serve
Fear, serve, cling, and swear
medium.explanation: The verse gives this order: fear the Lord, serve him, cleave to him, and swear by his name.

challenge.question: What does “He is thy praise” mean in the context of the verse?
answers: The Lord is the source of Israel’s honor and glory
Israel should praise itself
The Lord is only the name of a song
challenge.explanation: The verse continues by recalling the great and terrible things the Lord did for Israel, making him the source of its praise.

challenge.question: Why does the verse emphasize “which thine eyes have seen”?
answers: To say that the events were a dream
To emphasize that Israel personally experienced and saw the Lord’s works
To describe the color of the people’s eyes
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses that these were events the people themselves experienced and saw, not merely stories heard from others.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the verse mentioning fear, service, and clinging?
answers: Relationship with the Lord consists only of fear
Relationship with the Lord consists only of outward rituals
Relationship with the Lord includes feeling, action, and continuing loyalty
challenge.explanation: Fear expresses inner reverence, service expresses action, and clinging expresses ongoing loyalty and relationship.

questions.question: What does “He is thy praise” mean in the context of the verse?
answers: The Lord is the source of Israel’s honor and glory
Israel should praise itself
The Lord is only the name of a song
questions.explanation: The verse continues by recalling the great and terrible things the Lord did for Israel, making him the source of its praise.

questions.question: Why does the verse emphasize “which thine eyes have seen”?
answers: To say that the events were a dream

To describe the color of the people’s eyes
questions.explanation: The phrase stresses that these were events the people themselves experienced and saw, not merely stories heard from others.

answers: Relationship with the Lord consists only of fear

Relationship with the Lord includes feeling, action, and continuing loyalty
questions.explanation: Fear expresses inner reverence, service expresses action, and clinging expresses ongoing loyalty and relationship.

paragraphs.title: From Seventy People to a Great Nation

easy.question: How many people went down to Egypt with Israel’s ancestors?
answers: Seventy
One hundred
Twelve
easy.explanation: The verse says, “with threescore and ten persons” they went down to Egypt.

easy.question: Where did Israel’s ancestors go down?
answers: The wilderness
Egypt
Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The verse says that they went down into Egypt.

easy.question: What were the Israelites compared to later?
answers: The sand of the sea
The trees of the forest
The stars of heaven
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord made them “as the stars of heaven for multitude.”

medium.question: What change does the verse describe between the journey to Egypt and the later time?
answers: From a small family to a great multitude
From a great multitude to a small family
From Egypt to another land
medium.explanation: At first, seventy people went down to Egypt; later, they became very numerous.

medium.question: What is the connection between the number seventy and the image of the stars of heaven?
answers: Both describe where the people lived
The first describes a small beginning, while the second describes great multiplication
Both describe the number of years of exile
medium.explanation: Seventy describes the number who went down to Egypt, while the stars emphasize the great multitude they later became.

medium.question: In the phrase “with threescore and ten persons,” what does “persons” mean?
answers: People or individuals
Spirits only
Places of residence
medium.explanation: In the context of counting those who went to Egypt, “persons” means individual people—seventy people.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the comparison with the stars of heaven?
answers: The Israelites literally became stars
The Israelites multiplied into a very great number
They left the land and rose into the heavens
challenge.explanation: The comparison is a figure of speech for great multiplication, not a literal transformation into stars.

challenge.question: Who is presented in the verse as the one who caused the people to multiply?
answers: Pharaoh, king of Egypt
Israel’s ancestors
The Lord your God
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Lord your God made them as numerous as the stars of heaven.

challenge.question: Why does mentioning the descent into Egypt strengthen the meaning of the comparison with the stars?
answers: It highlights the contrast between a beginning of seventy people and a great multitude
It proves that all the stars are in Egypt
It explains why the Egyptians counted the stars
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts the small beginning of seventy people with the enormous multitude that followed, making the comparison more powerful.

questions.question: What can we infer from the comparison with the stars of heaven?
answers: The Israelites literally became stars
The Israelites multiplied into a very great number
They left the land and rose into the heavens
questions.explanation: The comparison is a figure of speech for great multiplication, not a literal transformation into stars.

questions.question: Who is presented in the verse as the one who caused the people to multiply?
answers: Pharaoh, king of Egypt
Israel’s ancestors
The Lord your God
questions.explanation: The verse says that the Lord your God made them as numerous as the stars of heaven.

questions.question: Why does mentioning the descent into Egypt strengthen the meaning of the comparison with the stars?
answers: It highlights the contrast between a beginning of seventy people and a great multitude
It proves that all the stars are in Egypt
It explains why the Egyptians counted the stars
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the small beginning of seventy people with the enormous multitude that followed, making the comparison more powerful.
